haiku: The paragraph runs a predictable four-part sequence (statistic, validation, reframe, prescription) in four sentences of similar length with no asides, fragments or digressions, which gives it a smooth, templated shape. The voice is conversational, though, so the machine feel is mostly in the structure rather than the wording.
sonnet: It is a compact four-sentence arc that goes statistic, then emotional reframe, then warning, then prescription, with every sentence the same medium length and a clean, even rhythm.
